questions.stem_text:
Which statement best describes the relationship between law and morality among non-
positivist legal theorists?

options.A: There is no relationship between law and morality.
options.B: Law is always in advance of moral ideas.
options.C: The law is inextricably bound up with morals.
options.D: Morality is generally in advance of the law.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: C - The law is inextricably bound up with morals.

questions.stem_text: Why is it important to separate the concept of punishment from its justification?

options.A: Because its justification depends on the concept employed.
options.B: Because any definition of punishment should be value-neutral.
options.C: Because the concept of punishment is controversial.
options.D: Because the practice of punishment is separate from its justification.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: B - Because any definition of punishment should be value-neutral.

questions.stem_text:
Dworkin contends that to every legal question there is only one right answer. Which
proposition below is most inconsistent with this claim?

options.A: In hard cases judges generally decide cases on the basis of rights.
options.B: The rights of the parties feature in the determination of most cases before the courts.
options.D: Judges seek the best 'fit' with constitutional and institutional history.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: C - Judges exercise strong discretion.

questions.stem_text:
Which proposition below is the most consistent with what Rawls claims the POP would opt
for in respect of 'social primary goods'?

options.A: The POP will choose wealth over a compassionate society.
options.B: The POP will choose equality over power.
options.D: The POP will choose to protect the disabled.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - The POP will choose wealth over a compassionate society.

questions.stem_text:
Soft positivism accepts that the rule of recognition may include moral criteria.' Which
proposition below is the most inconsistent with this description?

options.A: Incorporationism' accepts that judges may decide cases by reference to moral factors.'
options.B: A soft positivist rejects the role of morality in the description of law.
options.C: Sometimes the definition of law includes moral considerations.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: D - Judges lack strong discretion.

Discuss the key differences between conciliation and mediation in dispute resolution,
focusing on their processes, roles of the facilitators, and implications for the parties
involved.
questions.gold_answer:

while conciliation involves a commission, which proceeds to an impartial examination of
